intro: Lesson 31: Validation and authentication. To understand how validation checks and authentication make programs robust and secure

head: Check
Example
rows: Postcode or email has the right shape

questions.q: Write a presence check that keeps asking until a name is entered.
questions.a: name = input('Name: '); while name == '': name = input('Name: ')
questions.model: I do: name = input('Name: '). while name == '': print('Name required'); name = input('Name: '). The loop only ends when something is typed.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: write a sign-up program that validates a username (presence, 4 to 12 characters) and a password (at least 8 characters, contains a digit). Test with valid, boundary and invalid data.
questions.a: Loops for each rule; any(ch.isdigit() for ch in pw) or a loop for the digit; test table completed.
questions.model: The teacher writes the username length check: while len(u) < 4 or len(u) > 12: u = input('Username: ')

questions.q: Extend: why should a real system never store passwords as plain text?
questions.a: If data is stolen, passwords are exposed; systems store a hashed form.

questions.q: Stretch: why limit login attempts to three?
questions.a: To slow down guessing attacks (brute force).

questions.q: Back to our ponder: A form asks your age and someone types 250. Whose job is it to catch that: the user's or the program's?
questions.a: The program's: validation checks input is sensible before it is used.
